questions: How many C1 failures of the fixed 7B can P3-20 recover, and how many correct answers does it break, when it runs on every item rather than on the routed ones?
Does a stronger candidate stage inside P3-20 (BM25 plus deeper candidates, L2) recover more failures without more harm?
Can runtime signals rank items by expected repair utility (P(fix) - P(harm) - lambda * cost) well enough to keep route 1's gain with fewer P3-20 calls?
fixed: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct NF4 (rev a09a354) is not trained. C1 retrieval and prompt, Diagnosis, P60 and the Controller stay as in route 1. L2 changes only the candidate stage of P3-20.

step_1_p3_coverage.set: the quality sweep 6,000 Validation IDs (configs/controller/quality_sweep_v1.json); confirm 2,440 follows under the same rule
step_1_p3_coverage.input: the stored route-1 sweep records: C1 answer, Top-5, Diagnosis and frozen selection. C1 is not regenerated.
step_1_p3_coverage.action: route 1's P3-20 (CPU FP32 reranker, OMP/MKL 16 threads) as a forced decision on every item without a stored P3-20 outcome
step_1_p3_coverage.repro: P3-20 re-run on the first 200 items that have a stored outcome; final answer, status and final evidence agreement are reported
step_1_p3_coverage.labels: team judge on new (sample, answer) pairs with earlier labels reused; Validation gold is read locally only
step_1_p3_coverage.use: an intervention outcome for every item: recoverability analysis, gate training, and the L1 baseline for L2

step_2_l2: registered in a later commit before its GPU run: BM25 plus deeper candidates inside P3-20, reranker on GPU after a CPU equivalence check
step_3_gates: registered in a later commit before fitting: a pre-call repair-utility gate and a post-call acceptance gate, fitted on the sweep with cross-validation
evaluation: accuracy against P3-20 call rate, compared with random choice, p_fail order and route 1; fix and harm PR-AUC, calibration and false-skip rate. Confirm 2,440 is its third, disclosed use. Test runs only if a product change is adopted, as a further disclosed exposure.
metric: judge-assisted correctness. Unchanged answers count zero. On Test the RAG label wins on conflicts.
